topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: The weather's turned cold, the sort that seeps into your bones, just like the news that Olaf doesn’t recall the times we spent together. We used to run the hills, chasing the shadows of the setting sun, and he’d always say, “Mark my words, Jonas, one day we’ll venture beyond these fields.” The soil of our childhood holds so many seeds, yet it seems some have withered, taken by the wind. I still tend to my plot, sowing and reaping, but the rows feel a bit lonelier now. The church bells ring the same, but the sound doesn’t seem to carry as far. Maybe it’s the mist, or maybe it’s just the weight of silence. Saints know, it’s hard to see the harvest when the earth feels so bare.
